items.title: addyosmani/agent-skills
items.summary: addyosmani/agent-skills is a library that offers production-level engineering skills for artificial intelligence coding agents. Developed in the JavaScript language, this project aims to standardize the skills of agents in software processes.

snapshot.description: Production-grade engineering skills for AI coding agents. Production-grade engineering skills for AI coding agents.

items.title: we-promise/sure
items.summary: Sure, developed in the Ruby language, is a personal finance and asset management application open to everyone. Designed as an open-source platform, this project offers features that allow users to connect directly with financial advisors (CFP/CFA).

snapshot.description: The personal finance app for everyone (by everyone). The Maybe Finance (archived/abandoned repo) team spent most of 2021–2022 building a full-featured personal finance and wealth management app. It even included an “Ask an Advisor” feature that connected users with a real CFP/CFA — all included with your subscription.

items.title: homeassistant-ai/ha-mcp
items.summary: ha-mcp, developed for Home Assistant, allows you to configure and automate your smart home platform with artificial intelligence assistants like Claude and ChatGPT. Integrated via HACS, this tool works with full feature support on all Home Assistant installation types.

snapshot.description: Configure and automate Home Assistant with Claude, ChatGPT, and other AI assistants. The recommended way to run ha-mcp is the HA-MCP integration. It installs into Home Assistant through HACS (the built-in Marketplace on Home Assistant 2026.11+), runs the full server in-process, and works on every Home Assistant installation type — Home Assistant OS, Supervised, Container, and Core — with full feature parity.

items.title: tokio-rs/topcoat
items.summary: Topcoat is a modular and comprehensive Rust framework designed for developing web applications. Prioritizing simplicity and productivity, this structure aims to facilitate the full-stack application creation process.

snapshot.description: A batteries-included framework for building web apps. Topcoat is a modular, batteries-included Rust framework for building full-stack apps. It prioritizes simplicity and productivity. See Learn Topcoat to get started, or the Roadmap for what's coming next.

items.title: Amazon saves millions by replacing Sonnet 4.6 with Strands Decider
items.summary: Amazon engineers saved millions of dollars by replacing the Claude Sonnet 4.6 model used in their large-scale internal ticketing systems with the Strands Decider decision-making model. This change demonstrates the impact of cost-oriented model optimization in complex workflows.

snapshot.description: Two Amazon engineers swapped Claude Sonnet 4.6 for a decision model in one of the world's biggest internal ticketing systems.

items.title: AlphaProof Code
items.summary: AlphaProof Code, developed by Google DeepMind, is an AI system that combines mathematical reasoning and coding capabilities. This model aims to develop solutions in complex problem-solving processes by using code generation and logical verification methods.

items.title: .name Grandfathered
items.summary: The expiration of grandfathered rights for the .name domain extension has initiated a change process affecting current registrants. This situation requires users with this extension to comply with new rules regarding domain management and renewal policies.

items.title: Smart home devices should work without the internet
items.summary: This approach, which argues that smart home devices should operate without dependence on manufacturer servers, includes fundamental principles based on ten years of automation experience. It shares methods to be followed for building systems that maintain functionality even when the internet connection is lost.

snapshot.description: Rule one is that nothing in my house needs a vendor's server to work. The rest of the rules I follow after ten years of home automation, plus both talks I gave on it, slide by slide.

items.title: Blender 5.3 released with Gaussian Splat support
items.summary: Blender 5.3 has been released, adding Gaussian Splat support to the 3D modeling and animation software Blender. This update facilitates the use of Gaussian Splatting technology, which enables the transfer of real-world data into 3D environments.

items.title: onóna: Twin Embeddings with Tied Unembeddings
items.summary: Shared by Hugging Face, onóna presents a two-table parameterization that strengthens output expression while reducing the parameter cost of the weight tying method in language models. This method works by taking the average of two embedding tables in the Transformer architecture as input and combining the probability distributions of these tables at the output stage.

snapshot.description: Weight tying reduces the parameter cost of language models, but the usual tied output head is limited to a single softmax. We introduce onóna, a two-table parameterization that increases output expressiveness while preserving input-output weight sharing. The Transformer takes the average of two embedding tables as input, and the output head combines the softmax distributions defined by those same tables. items.title: RidgeFill: Training-Free Late-Layer Cache Fill for Faster Prefill
items.summary: RidgeFill offers a method to accelerate the prefill phase in large language models by shortening upper-layer computations. By predicting data from the model's lower layers using ridge regression, it optimizes the cache filling process even in untrained models.

snapshot.description: RidgeFill shortens prefill by not computing most of a model's upper layers for the prompt. The lower layers run exactly up to a split; from the split layer's state a per-layer map predicts every later layer's input, and each late layer writes its cache from that prediction. items.title: Creative Priming: Decoupling Process from Product to Escape the Creative Paradox
items.summary: The Creative Priming paper published on Hugging Face argues that creativity should be modeled as an open process rather than repeating past successes. The study focuses on how AI models can overcome the creativity paradox to develop new technologies and scientific theories.

snapshot.description: Many of the most consequential advances promised by AI, from curing diseases and inventing new technologies to formulating new scientific theories, are fundamentally creative acts. items.title: Click3R: Interactive Stereo 3D Reconstruction with Sparse Correspondence Clicks
items.summary: Click3R is an interactive framework developed to correct erroneous predictions of existing 3D reconstruction models. It allows for corrections by adding geometric constraints to the model through sparse correspondence clicks provided by users.

snapshot.description: Despite impressive progress, existing feed-forward large 3D reconstruction models produce a single, irrevocable prediction. When these models fail, there is no mechanism to correct their mistakes. To address this limitation, we introduce Click3R, a framework for interactive geometric correction of feed-forward models using sparse human correspondence clicks. items.title: LCM-Promo: An LLM-Based Uplift Model for Promotion Allocation
items.summary: LCM-Promo is an AI model based on a Large Commerce Model developed to predict users' purchase intent and their reactions to promotions. Trained with transaction data, this model aims to optimize promotion allocation processes by using session context.

snapshot.description: We present LCM-Promo, an LLM-based uplift model for promotion allocation. LCM-Promo is a task-specific Large Commerce Model (LCM): a finetuned LLM trained on transactional commerce data to predict user intent and promotion response. It learns monotonic promotion-response curves from production logs by interpreting single-token outputs as conversion-threshold probabilities, while conditioning on session context such as day and delivery shift.
